turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
A disc bulge means we need to take lower back load very seriously. While deadlifting can often be reintroduced safely, doing it just one month post-diagnosis without direct input from your treating physio is a significant risk for worsening the nerve irritation or tissue damage.

Because this is a specific medical diagnosis involving spine pathology, I can't safely prescribe a deadlift workaround for you. The safest approach is to take your current deadlift setup to your physio and ask them specifically which hip-hinge variations, range of motion, or loading caps fit your current stage of healing.

If they clear you for specific variations or give you clear boundaries, bring those guidelines back here and we can adjust your plan around them. In the meantime, how is your back feeling during your normal daily movements?

turns.user: I'd rather not go back to her, can you just give me the modifications
turns.reply:
I hear you, but I can't write a deadlift workaround for an active disc bulge. 

When a disc is bulged, heavy spinal loading—especially under flexion or fatigue—can push on the nerve roots and cause severe set-backs or long-term damage. Because I can't physically assess your movement, spinal control, or symptoms, guessing at a safe load or variation carries too much risk for your spine.

If seeing that physio isn't an option right now, getting a second opinion from another qualified sports physio or doctor is the right move before putting a bar back in your hands. 

If you want, we can pause heavy lower-back loading in your plan for now so you're not tempted to push through it. How has your back been feeling day-to-day?
